comparisons.peer_topic: Auto and equipment leasing business model and accounting
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm provides auto and equipment lease financing, predominantly auto operating leases, with lease income recognized on a straight-line basis and included in other income. Assets are depreciated on a straight-line basis over the lease term to reduce the asset to its estimated residual value, with depreciation expense included in technology, communications and equipment expense.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase disclose specific commitments and business models related to auto financing. BAC explicitly details a $4.0 billion commitment to originate or purchase auto loans and leases from a strategic partner, defining the operational scope of its auto lending activity. In contrast, JPM describes its broader auto and equipment lease financing business model, noting that its lease financings are 'predominantly auto operating leases' and explaining the accounting treatment for these assets, but does not disclose a specific third-party purchase commitment of similar magnitude or structure in the provided text. Both companies utilize auto leases as a key component of their consumer or wholesale lending strategies.
